author: Bill Ackman
title: Pershing Square Holdings 2025 Letter to Shareholders
headline: Ackman: NAV up 20.9% in 2025, Meta bought on its capex dip, and “constructive” on 2026.
summary: Pershing Square Holdings’ NAV rose 20.9% in 2025 (the shares 33.9%) against 17.9% for the S&P 500. Ackman argues the market’s rise rests on earnings growth, not speculation, and that index ownership plus leveraged short-term traders make even the largest stocks swing irrationally, which helps patient capital. He bought Meta after its capex-driven drop at about 20 times earnings, joining Alphabet and Amazon, and defends all three’s AI spending. Howard Hughes is to become “a modern-day Berkshire Hathaway”, starting with the $2.1 billion purchase of the insurer Vantage. He lists ten reasons 2026 could be a very strong economic year.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: New position in Meta after its October drop, bought at about 20 times earnings. Hilton was sold after seven years; Chipotle, Canadian Pacific and Nike were sold during 2025.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Higher capex at Alphabet, Amazon and Meta answers rising demand and should be applauded, not booed.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Howard Hughes, 47% owned together with the management company, is buying Vantage for $2.1 billion, with up to $1 billion of preferred equity from the fund.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac could re-rate above $40 a share if the plan Pershing Square published in November is followed.

risks.text: Leveraged short-term funds with stop-losses can force sharp, irrational drops after even a small disappointment.
Uber: investors fear autonomous vehicles from Tesla and Waymo will erode its network.
Universal Music: a possible share sale by Bolloré, a delayed US listing and worries about AI-made music.

quotes.text: When a business you own, managed by a management team you trust, announces a large increase in capital spending due to increased demand for its products or services, you should be applauding rather than booing.
Our long-term objective is to transform HHH into a modern-day Berkshire Hathaway
we are constructive on the current economic and market backdrop and on Pershing Square Holdings.
